chapters.title: Simple
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames simplicity as core plus compact: Commanders Intent, Southwest Airlines, the Daily Record, proverbs, schemas, and decision-paralysis research all point to forced prioritization that survives real choices.
chapters.coreMove: Strip a message to the one priority that should guide decisions when details collapse.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating simple as shorter wording, a slogan, or dumbed-down messaging.

chapters.title: Unexpected
chapters.sourcePressure: The source distinguishes attention from curiosity: surprise breaks a pattern, gap theory sustains attention, and examples like Nora Ephron, Sony pocket radio, and JFK moonshot keep the surprise tied to the core.
chapters.coreMove: Break the audiences expected pattern, then open a useful knowledge gap that pulls them toward the core.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing unexpected with shock, novelty, drama, or clickbait.

chapters.title: Concrete
chapters.sourcePressure: The source uses Aesops sour grapes, the Nature Conservancy, Jane Elliotts classroom exercise, Velcro Theory of Memory, and coordination language to show how abstract ideas need pictureable hooks.
chapters.coreMove: Turn an abstract claim into a shared visible reference people can picture, remember, and use together.
chapters.commonMisread: Adding vivid detail for decoration while leaving the working idea vague.
mustNotDriftInto: sensory writing for its own sake
overspecific anecdotes that bury the rule

chapters.title: Credible
chapters.sourcePressure: The source centers belief through proof, witnesses, vivid detail, anti-authority, and human-scale statistics, anchored by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren, Pam Laffin, and translated numbers.
chapters.coreMove: Move a claim from assertion into inspectable proof, witness, or human-scale evidence.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking credibility means adding credentials, citations, or bigger numbers.

chapters.title: Emotional
chapters.sourcePressure: The source treats emotion as making people care through one person, identity, dignity, self-interest, and meaning, with Floyd Lees Iraq dining example grounding morale and dignity.
chapters.coreMove: Make the consequence matter by tying it to one human stake, identity, dignity, or meaningful cost.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating emotion with sadness, hype, guilt, or inspirational language.

chapters.title: Stories
chapters.sourcePressure: The source is narrower here: stories carry lessons and practical meaning when the lesson is embedded in narrative, with challenge, connection, and creativity plots as supported labels.
chapters.coreMove: Embed the lesson in a sequence of choice and consequence so it can be retold without losing its action cue.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating any anecdote as useful simply because it is a story.
